props.title: The Loss of a Teardrop Diamond

sections.content: The Loss of a Teardrop Diamond (2008) represents a fascinating footnote in Tennessee Williams adaptation history - a previously unproduced 1957 screenplay finally brought to screen by director Jodie Markell. Bryce Dallas Howard stars as Fisher Willow, delivering a performance that channels the classic Williams heroines like Blanche DuBois from A Streetcar Named Desire (1951) and Maggie from Cat on a Hot Tin Roof (1958). The film captures Williams' signature Southern Gothic atmosphere, though it lacks the raw intensity that Elia Kazan brought to earlier adaptations.

movies.slug: Paul Newman and Elizabeth Taylor star in this sultry drama about a dysfunctional Southern family dealing with lies, greed and repression

sections.content: The film's 1920s Memphis setting aligns it with other Williams-inspired Southern period pieces like The Glass Menagerie (1950) and Summer and Smoke (1961). Howard's Fisher Willow embodies the archetypal Williams protagonist - privileged but troubled, fighting against societal constraints while harboring dark secrets. Her relationship with Chris Evans' Jimmy Dobyne echoes the class tensions found in Baby Doll (1956), though without that film's controversial edge. SUBHEAD: Tennessee Williams on Screen

While The Loss of a Teardrop Diamond never reaches the heights of classic Williams adaptations, it offers interesting parallels to later Southern Gothic films like The Help (2011) and Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil (1997). The film's emphasis on lost aristocracy and fading gentility connects it to modern explorations of the South like Winter's Bone (2010), though filtered through Williams' more melodramatic lens.
